svg.title: Circular-economy effects on European material production

cc:Work.dc:title: Circular-economy effects on European material production
cc:Work.dc:description: Percentage changes in European material production in 2050, with NDC above NDC+LTT and cement, iron and steel, and aluminium columns. Each policy category pairs OMNIA-ENGAGE on the left with hatched GCAM on the right. The medium and high EU-only CE scenarios are compared with each model's own no-CE scenario in the same pathway, sector and year: 100 × (CE output − no-CE output) / no-CE output. No CE is the zero reference by construction. The same percentage scale is used across all six panels. Markers identify observed values, including near-zero responses; labels are rounded to 0.1% and are not the plotting coordinates. Missing values remain gaps. Cement excludes clinker; OMNIA metal output sums primary and secondary routes, while GCAM uses its source-reported metal series. GCAM aluminium's route coverage is unconfirmed. Route contributions are exported as context but are not stacked in this figure, because GCAM has no matching route decomposition. Normalisation focuses on within-model CE responses and does not establish agreement in absolute production or energy levels, or harmonise the models' process boundaries. Historical bars are omitted because these are matched-year CE contrasts. OMNIA sums EUE, EUM and EUW; GCAM selects its EU-27 aggregate once. The OMNIA regions include some small non-EU countries and territories. Only medium/high CE applied in the EU enters; EU+ cases are excluded. Raw source quantities, reference totals, exact variables, regions and calculation coefficients accompany every result. A missing, nonfinite or nonpositive reference makes the response undefined.
